findings: Check-then-insert TOCTOU race in signup(): two concurrent signup calls for the same email can both pass the SELECT check before either INSERT commits, producing duplicate accounts, because there is no transaction, lock, or unique index enforcing it.
No UNIQUE constraint exists on users.email in the schema, so the application-level 'email taken' check is the only guard against duplicates, and it is not atomic.

phone is declared TEXT NULL in the schema but the User TypeScript interface declares phone: string as required/non-nullable -- a nullability mismatch that lets a null value silently violate the type contract.
listActiveUsers() never filters on deleted_at IS NULL despite its name, so soft-deleted users are returned as if they were active.

The email-uniqueness check in signup() is an exact, case-sensitive string comparison (WHERE email=$1) with no normalization, so equivalent emails differing only in case or whitespace are treated as distinct and can both be registered.

Because signup()'s 'email taken' check queries all rows regardless of deleted_at, a previously soft-deleted account's email permanently blocks re-signup with that same email -- an interaction between soft-delete and uniqueness that's undefined and untested.
